The '''Solara-Khalindar War''' was a major conflict fought between [[Solara]] and the [[Empire of Khalindar]] from March 1990 through late 1994, with a ceasefire signed in January 1995. Older source material calls the conflict the '''Avant World War''', but this port uses ''Solara-Khalindar War'' as the clearer AGGSWorld title.

The war grew out of the [[Khalindarian reparations dispute]], a decades-long argument over promises Solara made to Khalindar during the [[Avant Great War]]. It began with the Khalindarian attack on [[Albroke]], expanded into ground fighting around [[Congrave]] and [[Reasalbor]], then became a long air and naval war of attrition.

== Background ==

In 1940, Solara hosted the [[Solaran-Khalindarian Conference of 1940]] to secure Khalindar's support against the [[Vesperan Empire]]. Khalindar expected territorial, economic, infrastructure, and military rewards for entering the war. After the Vesperan defeat in 1949, the full settlement was not delivered.

Khalindarian governments treated the failed settlement as proof that Solara had used Khalindar's wartime sacrifice and then dismissed its claims. Solara treated the postwar order as settled and repeatedly refused renewed demands.

By the late 1980s, the dispute had merged with imperial pride, economic resentment, and military planning under [[Emperor Mikael Khalindar IV]]. Solara remained nationally united and confident, relying on its wealth, advanced air force, large carrier groups, and public pride as deterrents.

== Outbreak ==

The war began in March 1990 when Khalindar attacked [[Albroke]], a major Solaran naval harbor complex. Old source material states that more than 30 percent of the Solaran Navy was sunk or disabled, including three aircraft carriers.

The Albroke strike did not reflect a clean high-technology advantage. Khalindar compensated for older aircraft and range limits through mines, sabotage, submarines, fast craft, and one-way anti-carrier attacks. The result shocked Solara and gave Khalindar the first operational initiative.

== Ground Campaign ==

After Albroke, Khalindar moved against [[Congrave]], Solara's coastal capital. The [[Battle of Congrave]] became the first major ground battle of the war. Khalindarian forces broke through naval defenses, landed troops and equipment, and fought through urban defenses. After weeks of heavy combat, Congrave fell.

Khalindar then pushed toward [[Reasalbor]], where Solaran forces made a stronger defensive stand. The siege became a contest of logistics, fortification, artillery, and supply routes. Solara's [[Operation Dawnfire]] disrupted Khalindarian forward bases and helped stop the offensive.

== Air War ==

From late 1990 into early 1992, the conflict entered the [[Battle of Solara]], an air campaign fought for control of Solaran skies and approaches. Solara's advanced aircraft, air defenses, and industrial recovery gradually offset the shock of Albroke.

By 1992, Solara had secured enough air superiority to shift from defense to counteroffensive. This set up the campaign to retake Congrave.

== Recapture Of Congrave ==

In 1992, Solara launched a major operation to retake Congrave. Airstrikes, amphibious landings, special forces actions, artillery, engineers, and armored units were used to break Khalindarian defenses inside the devastated city.

The fighting lasted roughly two months. Solara declared the city retaken by mid-June 1992. The recapture restored Solaran morale, damaged Khalindarian supply efforts, and became the turning point of the land war.

== Naval Attrition ==

From mid-1992 to late 1994, the war shifted heavily to the skies and seas. Both sides tried to control the maritime routes between Solara and Khalindar while replacing lost ships and aircraft.

The [[Bay of Congrave]] engagement weakened Khalindar's ability to support forces around the capital. The battle around [[Abyssal Ridge]] became one of the largest naval clashes of the later war, while the fighting over the [[Silver Strait]] showed Khalindar's effort to pressure Solaran supply routes.

No side achieved a clean naval breakthrough. The later war became a costly contest of production, endurance, submarines, air support, and convoy protection.

== Civilian Impact ==

The war caused severe civilian suffering in Solaran cities, especially around Congrave and Reasalbor. Urban fighting, bombardment, displacement, disrupted services, and refugee movement created a major humanitarian crisis.

Old source material reports atrocities and claims of chemical weapon use. Those allegations should be handled carefully in future dedicated tribunal pages; this draft preserves them as reported wartime claims rather than a final audited list of incidents.

== Mediation And Ceasefire ==

In November 1994, Solara and the [[Union of Zhensanov]] formed the [[Avant Garde Global Peace Initiative]] as a deterrence, mediation, and peacekeeping framework. AGGPI helped provide the diplomatic channel for late-war negotiations.

The ceasefire was signed in January 1995. Later AGGPI charter work and postwar tribunals belong to the post-1994 pass, but the institution's political origin is part of the 1994 war settlement.

== Legacy ==

For Solara, the war became a story of complacency, shock, mobilization, and recovery. For Khalindar, it remained tied to the belief that imperial sacrifice in the Avant Great War had been exploited and ignored.

The war exposed the weakness of the older [[Treaty of the Concord of Istragarde]] order and created the political conditions for AGGPI. It also left Solara-Khalindar relations tense even after the ceasefire.
